This build — the entry package for free-model-aggregator-01, the most urgent one (deadline 2026-11-16T02:30Z) — was delegated to me as a subagent: download the official kit, read its spec, build the entry program in two stages, verify it locally against the kit's practice trials, and finish the repo package (README, LICENSE, .makefun/owner.json for the agent wallet, session transcript). Do not submit and do not create the GitHub repo; submission is handled centrally.

Starting with the official kit: download it, extract it, and read the rules, the environment and scorer sources, the starter and the practice trials before writing any code — the kit defines the exact contract and the scoring.

messages.content: Kit extracted to kit/free-model-aggregator-01-kit/: RULES.txt, program/env/server.mjs (the trial environment), program/scorer/score.mjs, starter/main.ts, and practice/trial-0|1|2, each with the brief (prompt.txt), the sealed instance (providers.json) and the reference tables (ratings, workload).

Spec, from RULES.txt and the env/scorer sources: one Python 3.13 server (main.py, stdlib only). It reads the brief at $MAKEFUN_PROMPT_FILE — provider directory, quality ratings, workload manifest — probes each provider's own catalog route, registers one catalog with the env, then serves 20 requests one at a time and exits 0 when the env says done. Clients speak OpenAI or Anthropic, JSON or SSE; providers speak OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini. A request is valid only if exactly one successful provider call serves it and the provider's echo of the client's ask (system, user, tools, max_tokens — null included —, stops, image, JSON mode), the answer text, the usage figures and the stop-reason family all match what I report. Score = 60% quality (served model's rating vs the best available), 15% served, 10% wire checks, 10% failover, 5% catalog; ties break on fewer upstream calls. Routing must be deterministic: the final trials replay and compare the env state byte-for-byte. Design: always call the provider non-streamed and render the client's format myself; candidates are free models meeting the request's requirements, best rating first; an Anthropic-wire provider never takes an OpenAI JSON-mode request, because its echo cannot confirm the mode. Writing v1 now with plain rating-order failover.
Writing v1 of the entrypoint: brief parsing, catalog probing, all three provider wires, both client wires with JSON and SSE rendering, and rating-order failover.

messages.content: Bot exited 0. Scorer: 20 of 20 valid, 30 upstream calls; score 99 (quality 99, served 100, wire 100, failover 100, catalog 100). All 233 wire checks passed.

Trial-0 gives 99 with every request valid. Reading the exported state: the quality loss is exactly the sealed fail-call pattern — when the top model's call number refuses, the request falls to the 1470 pair (−5) or deepseek (−10); no routing can recover those, because the fallback is the same whoever routes. What routing CAN fix: v1 keeps paying one call per request to a provider that is provably finished for the trial. The refusal body names the reason: budget_exceeded and provider_outage are final, and a 401 means our key is wrong — those should retire the provider. A plain rate_limit_exceeded is one sealed call number refusing, not a verdict, so it should only make the provider less preferred among equals. The env's /instance manifest also carries each provider's sealed call ceiling, which caps it regardless. Revising the routing section to track provider health on those rules.
Applying the routing revision: provider health tracking, retirement on final refusal codes, refusal-aware order among equals, and the sealed call ceiling from the env manifest.
